operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers: Race_ID, Track_ID, Year_Opened, Name, Class, Date — must be double-quoted in generated SQL; column lookup case-insensitive.
race.Track_ID declared TEXT but FK to track.Track_ID declared INT: type-affinity mismatch across the FK edge; parent values are integers, child stores them as text ('1','2',...).
race.Track_ID has 6 distinct over 7 rows (one duplicate) — FK child is non-unique, parent is unique PK; fine, but child draws with replacement.
race.Date is TEXT holding free-form human dates ('January 26 January 27', 'March 29', 'April 19') — NOT ISO, NOT parseable by TS Date templates; dispatches to String fuzzer, not Date.
race.Class has only 2 distinct values ('DP/GT','GT') — low-cardinality enum-like text; TS String fuzzer will not reproduce this.
track.Seating and track.Year_Opened declared REAL, storage real, values are whole numbers (92000.0, 1997.0) — Number fuzzer with scale from REAL (no args) will emit floats.
track.Year_Opened is a year stored as REAL, not declared YEAR — dispatches to Number, not the year fuzzer.
Tiny tables (race=7, track=9 rows): choose_table_sizes will produce sizes far larger than originals; original_values sampling k=min(5,len) is fine.
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE constraints beyond PKs — insert failures only from PK collisions.
Self-references: none. Composite keys: none. Dangling FKs: none (parent_exists true).
Table order: track (level 0) before race (level 1) — FK fill works in one pass.
race.Name values contain dots, spaces, digits ('RumBum.com 250', 'Bosch Engineering 250 at VIR') — String fuzzer charset a-zA-Z 0-9() will not match punctuation like '.' or '/'.
operator_ts_expectations: Race_ID, Track_ID (track): Number fuzzer, int, scale 0, range [-1,1] plus perturbation — will generate tiny ints, mostly colliding with PK uniqueness filter; distinct count collapses.
race.Track_ID: String fuzzer (declared TEXT) but FK fill overrides — draws from track.Track_ID final values with replacement, so text '1'..'9' style; consistent with parent.

race.Name, track.Name, track.Location: String fuzzer, length range from min/max of 5 sampled originals, charset a-zA-Z 0-9() — plausible-looking but not real track names; FN risk when gold filters on specific names.
race.Class: String fuzzer over 2 originals — will emit random strings, not 'DP/GT'/'GT'; gold queries filtering Class='GT' will get empty or wrong results -> FN.
race.Date: String fuzzer (TEXT, not date-dispatched) — will emit random strings, never 'January 26' style; gold date predicates (LIKE '%January%', month extraction) will miss -> FN.

track.Seating, track.Year_Opened: Number fuzzer scale 0 (REAL, no args -> scale 0, precision 0), range [-1,1] plus +-1/+-2 perturbation — will NOT produce 92000 or 1997; gold range predicates (Seating>50000, Year_Opened>1990) will be empty -> FN.
Number fuzzer list_max quirk: upper end overwritten to full-range max, so even with originals the fresh draws dominate small ranges.

PK uniqueness filter (sample_fresh_primary_keys) on Race_ID/Track_ID with tiny int range will drop most rows -> small effective table sizes, possibly 0-2 rows -> FP from missing ties/duplicates in aggregates.
String contaminate (0.5 prob) adds/drops chars — further degrades name/class/date plausibility.
No NOT NULL/CHECK enforcement: NULLs may appear in columns that were 0% null originally (String/Number samplers can emit None via element dropout) -> gold IS NOT NULL predicates change cardinality.
FK fill draws from parent FINAL filtered values; if track PK filter leaves few rows, race.Track_ID gets few distinct -> join cardinality collapses -> FP on COUNT/aggregate queries.
Low original distinct (Class=2, Track_ID=6) means literal pool from train SQL is the main source of plausible values; without it TS is near-random.
